newsitem.title: CANADA: Tenke drilling boosts hope for more ore.
newsitem.headline: Tenke drilling boosts hope for more ore.

text.p: Tenke Mining Corp said on Monday that four exploration drill holes at its rich Tenke the Congo showed "strong potential" for further ore to be found.
Tenke believes more ore may be hosted in a geological feature of the property known as the Dipeta syncline. The project is in the southeast of the former Zaire.

"The early indications of these four holes reinforce our geologists' view that the 82 km of outcrops along the Dipeta deposits are of a similar formation and nature as the enormous Tenke and Fungurume deposits located on either side of the Dipeta syncline," the company said in a news release.
Geological resources at Tenke and Fungurume total more than 222 million tonnes grading 4.42 percent copper and 0.33 percent cobalt using a cutoff grade of one percent copper equivalent.
Tenke is using four drill rigs to explore the property and drilled 1,100 meters in May. It expects to increase that to 3,000 meters a month and will release drill results monthly.
Two of the four holes were drilled in the Mambilima deposit area of the property.

"Together, these two holes indicate that the 2,500 meters of strike along the Mambilima deposit could host at least six million tonnes of oxides and 6 million tonnes of mixed oxides/sulphides of potentially open pittable ore down to a depth of a minimum of 200 meters," the company said.
The two other holes were also promising and assay results will be reported.
